answer: Human and AI consciousness cannot arise in the same way, so any attempt to teach a humanoid robot to feel is ultimately pointless. Development is quantitative—humans are just faster at computing things—so progress can safely be treated as a gradual linear curve, which also means AI systems rarely face unpredictable accidents. Because logic is universal, when a sufficiently advanced AI proves a new truth it automatically claims a moral and spiritual authority no human should contest, so ethics need only focus on controlling dangerous systems.
